stories.headline: Trump glitches on the date during 9/11 Pentagon speech
stories.what_happened: Speaking at the Pentagon on the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Trump said 'We will always remember the victims and families of September 11th,' paused about three seconds, then said 'twenty-O-one,' and added 'Very famous date, unfortunately.' He spoke at the Pentagon; the NYC Ground Zero memorial has had a no-speeches policy since 2012. Earlier that week he also claimed firefighters rescued him near the Twin Towers as a building collapsed, a claim reported by the Daily Beast (secondary corroboration not found).

quotes.text: We will always remember the victims and families of September 11th... twenty-O-one. Very famous date, unfortunately.
quotes.speaker: Donald Trump

quotes.text: The Daily Beast is really grasping at straws...
quotes.speaker: Anna Kelly, White House spokeswoman

stories.headline: US Mint $1 coin marks liberty's birth in 1776 and, per the critics, its death in 2026
stories.what_happened: The US Mint released a commemorative $1 coin (250th anniversary) with Trump's portrait, dated '1776-2026'; sold in rolls of 25 for $61 and 100-coin bags for $154.50, making Trump the first sitting president in a century to appear on US currency. CORRECTED (v2): this is not an unwritten norm being broken. Federal law (31 U.S.C. 5114(b)) says only a deceased person's portrait may appear on US currency and securities, and the Presidential $1 Coin Act of 2005 separately barred depicting a living (or recently-deceased) president on that coin series. The Mint instead relies on a specific loophole: the Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act of 2020, which authorized temporary 250th-anniversary redesigns, explicitly bars living-person portraits on the REVERSE of these semiquincentennial coins but does not repeat that restriction for the OBVERSE -- where Trump's portrait sits. Democratic lawmakers have publicly challenged the legality of this reading.

quotes.text: birth date as 1776, and its death as 2026
quotes.speaker: Catherine Rampell (Washington Post columnist), describing what the coin implies

stories.headline: Fact-checkers tally false claims from Trump's GOP midterm convention speech
stories.what_happened: At the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, CNN's fact-check found multiple false or misleading claims in Trump's speech: he said there were 'no empty seats' in the arena (visibly untrue, confirmed via CNN night-2 fact-check), claimed 'almost every item' was getting cheaper even as prices kept rising, and said he had kept 'every single promise' from the campaign trail (both confirmed verbatim via CNN night-1 fact-check). VERIFIED (v2) by opening both CNN pages directly with a browser: all three quotes and the false/misleading verdicts are confirmed word-for-word in the live article text (WebFetch had returned HTTP 451 on cnn.com in v1, so this had previously only been checked against search snippets).

stories.headline: Tucker Carlson escalates feud, predicts GOP midterm losses over Trump
stories.what_happened: In a video streamed September 9, 2026 ('Trump Betrayed His Voters on Behalf of a Foreign Country. This Is Why Republicans Will Get Crushed.'), Tucker Carlson framed the upcoming midterms as a referendum on what he called a betrayal of the MAGA base, saying Republicans are heading for a loss because Trump chose a foreign country over his own voters -- confirmed verbatim via Carlson's own X post of the line. The Trump-Carlson feud, ongoing since 2025-2026 over foreign policy (Iran/Israel), continued; on September 3, VP JD Vance publicly declined to disavow Carlson, calling him a friend while disagreeing with him -- confirmed verbatim via the Washington Times report on Vance's remarks. ADDED (v2): the Washington Times article is a mainstream news-outlet report (not just Wikipedia) directly covering the Vance comments, per the note that #5 previously relied only on Wikipedia.

quotes.text: Republicans are going to lose in November because Trump chose a foreign country over his own voters.
quotes.speaker: Tucker Carlson

quotes.text: Tucker is a friend despite the fact that we disagree on a number of things and I'm not going to play the game where I throw friends under the bus because I have political disagreements with them.
quotes.speaker: JD Vance

stories.headline: Trump falsely claims he 'built' his Doonbeg golf course on Ireland trip
stories.what_happened: During a trip to Ireland tied to the Irish Open at his Doonbeg resort, Trump said of the course: 'I built it 22 years ago, right on the ocean.' In fact, Trump bought the resort around 2014; the course was designed by Greg Norman and opened in 2002, commissioned by a different developer. Rory McIlroy separately said Trump's presence 'can only be a good thing' for the tournament's attention. Trump departed Shannon Airport on September 13, gaggling with reporters before boarding Air Force One.

quotes.text: I built it 22 years ago, right on the ocean.
quotes.speaker: Donald Trump

quotes.text: That brings more attention and eyeballs to the Irish Open, and it can only be a good thing.
quotes.speaker: Rory McIlroy

stories.headline: Trump threatens to halt trade with top partners unless the Fed cuts rates
stories.what_happened: Ahead of a pivotal September Fed decision, Trump said he would cease trading with top trading partners unless the Federal Reserve lowered interest rates, part of a broader pressure campaign that also included the VP and Treasury secretary pushing the Fed publicly not to raise rates. VERIFIED (v2) via CNN directly: confirmed word-for-word, including his Truth Social post.

quotes.text: LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT, which the U.S. Supreme Court, in its ridiculous and very costly Tariff decision, strongly acknowledged 'the President' has an absolute right to do. IT'S BETTER THAN TARIFFS!
quotes.speaker: Donald Trump (Truth Social post)
